title: Review of c08's NRCH crystal-growth negative: replicates on fresh seed 6; net production (phi_t=-0.3) adds transient splits that are matched by merges, then the swimmer lattice freezes at a constant count
summary: Fresh seed 6 (192^2, T=6000, the author's command) of the strongest net-production arm (phi0=-0.4, phi_t=-0.3, u=1.5e-3) and of the default no-net-production world. Net production: 93 splits against 83 merges, 2 persistent splits, max generation 1; the swimmer count is constant at 23 from t~1950 to 6000 while the bodies lock into a polar travelling lattice (sheet.png from t~2000; best track 72.8 body lengths). Default: 52 splits, 30 merges, 1 persistent split, constant at 22 from t~2825. So net production roughly doubles transient split/merge churn but leaves no lasting division and the same lattice, as the finding says.

observations.D: net_prod/seed6/FACTS.md: splits 93, merges 83, persistent splits 2, max generation 1; counts_seed6.txt: 23 swimmers constant from t~1950 to 6000 (default: 22 from t~2825)

controls_run.D: default/seed6 (phi_t = phi0, no net production), same seed and command

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, one of the three net-production arms. labkit's split counts in this colliding lattice-forming population are mostly fragment-merge churn during the transient.
